$comment: Copy this file to <id>.json and fill it in. Files starting with _ are not records.
Delete every key you do not need -- an unknown or wrongly-present key is an error, and
that is on purpose: it is how a half-filled record gets caught instead of shipped.
Which optional keys you keep depends on confidence and kind:
confidence measured   -> keep measured_on, environment, repro   (required)
confidence documented -> keep sources                           (required); delete the three above
confidence inferred   -> keep inferred_from                     (required); delete the three above
confidence unverified -> delete all of the above
kind behaviour        -> DELETE status, fix, why_not_closed
kind trap|limitation  -> keep status; closed needs fix, open_recorded needs why_not_closed
docs/<file>.md#<heading anchor>   the prose is already written; both must exist
issue:<number>                    a report is the source
record                            this record is the first place it is written down
The last two are for an observation with no prose yet. Do not write a stub heading just
to satisfy the first shape -- the index counts records with no prose, so say so instead.
Never guess an environment value. Write "unrecorded".
measured_on does NOT take "unrecorded": if you cannot date it, it is not a measurement.
title: one line, what goes wrong
summary: what happens, in a few sentences. No measurement words unless confidence is measured.
repro: what you ran, and what came back
why_not_closed: why it is being left open

detection.note: why a machine cannot check this one. When checkable is true, delete this and give
